hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis, surgery, or hospital stay in Yuba City goes wrong, sorting out what happened can feel overwhelming on top of recovery. LawProactive connects you with an independent attorney who can look at the medical record and tell you honestly whether something more than a bad outcome occurred.

about.title: Yuba City Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Sutter County residents rely on a handful of local hospitals and clinics for everything from emergency care to childbirth, and most visits go the way they should. But when a provider misses a clear warning sign, operates on the wrong site, or sends a patient home with the wrong medication, the harm can be lasting. California law makes these cases genuinely difficult to bring: MICRA requires a qualified medical expert to back up the claim, imposes a 90-day pre-suit notice before filing, and sets tight, discovery-based deadlines. A bad result by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred — the law asks whether the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your case; we simply connect Yuba City residents with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can review the medical file and explain your options in plain terms.
commonInjuries: Delayed or missed diagnosis of a serious condition
Birth injuries to mother or newborn
Failure to monitor a patient after treatment

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, plus a required 90-day notice before a lawsuit can even be filed.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: MICRA cases typically need a qualified medical expert willing to say the care fell below accepted standards — an attorney can help determine if that threshold is met.

items.title: Damages Caps That Change Yearly
items.desc: Non-economic damages in California malpractice cases are capped by statute, but that cap rises each year, which affects how a claim is valued and negotiated.

items.question: I had a bad outcome from surgery in Yuba City — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing. An attorney reviewing the medical records can help determine whether the standard of care was actually breached.

items.question: How long do I have to act after a medical error in Sutter County?
items.answer: Generally you have one year from when you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a mandatory 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for you. We don't practice law ourselves — we simply help you find someone who can evaluate your situation.
